A U-admissible Chow lemma (the run cites Raynaud 1972, Ch. 4 §4 Prop. 5; locator not opened by me) gives a blowup X_1 -> X with centre disjoint from the quasi-projective open N containing Y, X_1 projective; its normalization X' -> X is an isomorphism over N, so the boundary Y' = q^{-1}(Y) and its divisorial valuations are those of Y, and all exceptional divisors lie over X - N, inside U' where pulled-back covers are étale. A connected cover of the normal X - Y stays connected on U' (same generic fibre), so Q(X',Y') ->> Q(X,Y), and Q(X',Y') is finitely generated by the projective case of D:fixed-boundary-positive. The one-point case holds since a point has an affine neighbourhood (a finite set of points need not, on a non-projective scheme, and the run claims only one point). This repairs the Chow step of 29/066 (F12) whenever the omitted set has a quasi-projective neighbourhood.
